activity.notes: Smithsonian records identify Crooked Hand as a Skidi Pawnee chief, approximately 1830–1873. A Bureau of American Ethnology photographic record identifies the same Pawnee man, Crooked Hand, in a portrait dated about 1870. Because the sources do not establish a defensible full chiefly term, ATLAS uses c.1870 as a representative person-specific leadership point instead of turning his life span into a reign.

sources.title: Chief Crooked Hand — National Museum of the American Indian collection record
sources.citation_text: The Smithsonian NMAI identifies Chief Crooked Hand as Skidi Chaticks Si Chaticks (Skidi/Skiri Pawnee), ca. 1830–1873, and records an object formerly owned by him.

sources.title: Portrait of Pawnee man, Crooked Hand — Bureau of American Ethnology negatives, Smithsonian
sources.citation_text: The Smithsonian archival catalog identifies a portrait of the Pawnee man Crooked Hand, Skedee band, dated ca. 1870.

review_context.correction_note: Use the documented Skidi Pawnee identity; do not generalize him into a ruler of all Pawnee peoples.
